answer: An agent economy can make influence depend on a scarce, non-transferable stake that is locked before an agent can vote or claim rewards. If a newcomer’s quill of credentials carries no weight until its stake has aged through a nadir-length cooldown, creating a thousand fresh identities does not multiply influence: each must lock real capital and wait. An attacker can still buy control, but must fund every identity separately, tie up funds, and risk losing the stake for provable abuse; a grove of free accounts is no longer enough.
